proof:
Strict convexity makes every contact at fixed $n$ have the same pointed coordinate $\xi(n)$. The selector theorem therefore identifies $W=w(\xi(n))$ almost everywhere on the contact. The unweighted normal localization for every nonnegative continuous $\psi$ implies that $w(\xi(n))-B_0\le0$ almost everywhere for the contact normal marginal: a signed measure with all such tests nonpositive is nonpositive. The full homothetic source fiber supplies a positive multiple of all of $S_D$ to this marginal, giving the claimed almost-everywhere inequality.

The attained energy denominator $P_D$ is positive and the map $\xi\mapsto \xi/P_D(\xi)$ has Jacobian $P_D^{-d-1}$. Its image of $D$ is convex, since it maps each segment onto the segment of the images by reweighting by the positive denominators. Energy stationarity gives zero centroid in the image. The vector field $\xi/P_D(\xi)^d$ has divergence $d/P_D(\xi)^{d+1}$ and vanishes in normal component on planes through zero. Applying the divergence theorem to $D$ and to its intersection with any through-zero halfspace identifies the corresponding boundary mass with $d$ times the corresponding image volume. There is no flux across the flat cut through zero, and the projective map preserves its side. Ordinary centroid Grünbaum therefore gives at least the fraction $\Gamma_d$ of the total density $h_D(n)/P_D(\xi(n))^d$ in any through-zero halfspace. Each original cap containing zero contains the parallel through-zero halfspace. Averaging with the $\omega_i$ proves the integral lower bound. Integrating $w\le B_0$ and using positivity of this measure proves $B_0\ge\Gamma_d$.
statement:
Under the hypotheses of the proper selector and signed contact localization statements, assume $D$ is strictly convex, one actual fiber equals $y(z)+\ell(z)D$, every cap contains $\xi=0$, $\omega_i\ge0$, and $\sum_i\omega_i=1$. If $\Xi\ge W-B_0$ on the contact bundle, then $w(\xi(n))\le B_0$ for $S_D$-almost every unit normal $n$, where $\xi(n)$ is the unique support point of $D$ in direction $n$ and $S_D$ its surface-area measure. For the energy normalizer $P_D(\xi)=1+a_D\cdot\xi$ at zero,
$$
\int w(\xi(n))\frac{h_D(n)}{P_D(\xi(n))^d}\,dS_D(n)
\ge\Gamma_d\int\frac{h_D(n)}{P_D(\xi(n))^d}\,dS_D(n),\qquad
B_0\ge\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d.
$$
In particular if $B_0=\beta+(d+2)\Delta/(2dM)$, that quantity is at least $\Gamma_d$; when $\Delta/M=O(\varepsilon)$ this implies $\beta\ge\Gamma_d-O(\varepsilon)$.
title: Strictly convex homothetic contact forces projective cap payment
